name: Armenia
summary: An ancient nation in the Caucasus, the first to adopt Christianity as a state religion (301); briefly independent (1918–20), Soviet, then independent again in 1991.

location.value: In the South Caucasus; about 29,700 km².

terrain.value: Highlands around the mountains of Ararat, with the high-altitude Lake Sevan.

disasters.value: The 1988 Spitak earthquake killed more than 25,000 people and left 500,000 homeless; its effects are still felt.

urbanisation.value: Yerevan is the capital, largest city and financial centre.

disease.value: Basic health care is good, with life expectancy around 75 years.

migration.value: A large diaspora (8 million by some estimates) that far outnumbers the 3 million people in Armenia.

economicBase.value: Mining, an active information technology sector and investment from Armenians abroad.

tradeRoutes.value: Its borders with Turkey and Azerbaijan are under a severe blockade.

wealth.value: A developing country, 69th on the Human Development Index (2023).

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

keyRulers.value: Armenia’s leaders since independence in 1991 are not named here.

succession.value: Elections have been held since independence, with changes of government in 2018.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Armed forces; Russia keeps a military base at Gyumri.

majorWars.value: The First Nagorno-Karabakh War (ended 1994), the six-week war of 2020 and Azerbaijan's 2023 offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh.

territoryChange.value: Armenia supported the breakaway Republic of Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh) until Azerbaijan reincorporated the region in 2023.

alliancesRivals.value: Turkey closed its border with Armenia in 1993; ties with its long-time ally Russia worsened after 2023.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: A strong science tradition, including the Armenian Academy of Sciences.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Mountain roads and a railway to Georgia, with a long closed border to Turkey and Azerbaijan.

religion.value: The Armenian Apostolic Church, the world's oldest national church, is the main religious establishment.

languageWriting.value: Armenian, the only official language, has its own alphabet created by Mesrop Mashtots.

artsArchitecture.value: Medieval monasteries such as Geghard and Tatev, and distinctive khachkar stone crosses.

socialStructure.value: About 98% ethnic Armenian at the start of the 21st century, with a small Yazidi minority.

sharedIdentity.value: Christianity (the state religion since 301) and the Armenian alphabet are cornerstones of Armenian identity.

dailyLife.value: Many families eat lavash (flatbread) and khorovats (barbecue).

colonisation.value: Eastern Armenia was conquered by the Russian Empire by the 19th century; by 1920 it was part of the Soviet Union, until independence in 1991.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Armenia continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
